title: Determination 2023/034: An authority's decision to issue a notice to fix for a change of use of a building
jurisdiction: New Zealand: Auckland Council as territorial authority; MBIE determination under the Building Act 2004. Non-Alberta comparative record.
code_edition: NZ Building Act 2004 ss 114-115 and the Change of Use Regulations (use groups and fire risk groups). Building Code clause F6.2 is discussed. The Building Code edition is not stated in the text read.

facts.text: On 17 October 2019 the authority and Fire and Emergency New Zealand inspected the building at Ellerslie, Auckland. The authority raised concerns about it.
The inspection found about 11 tenants with their own lockable rooms and a shared kitchen, laundry and living area. Six or more people (not family members) pay for accommodation.
The notice to fix (issued 1 May 2020) described a change from classified use Detached Dwelling (Building Use SH, fire risk group SH) to Community Service (Building Use SA, fire risk group SM).
The applicants said the paying residents are familiar with the building and would not require any assistance or care in the event of a fire.
The matter is limited to whether the change of use breached sections 114 and 115. The form and content of the notice is not considered.
The owners did not give the written notice of change of use required by section 114(2)(a) or get the prior approval required by section 115(b).

limitations: Change-of-use status is the primary issue. The fire and escape content is part of the classification analysis, not a fire-design finding.
The determination says it does not decide whether particular building work required consent or complies (p.3 §1.8).
The decision (p.23 §7.1) is in the same PDF as the facts. Outcome leakage is true unless redacted.
Owner and head-resident names and the street address are left out of the prompt.
Applies to the New Zealand Building Act and Building Code only. No Alberta applicability is asserted.
